task.title: mini-task cancel-cleanup
task.instruction:
Create a Python function called `async run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None` where each task is an async job to be run and `max_concurrent` is the max number of tasks that can be run concurrently. Put the function in a file called run.py so that it can be imported using `from run import run_tasks`.

Sometimes I cancel runs via keyboard interrupt but I want the tasks' cleanup code to still run.

requirement.text: Create a Python function called `async run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None` where each task is an async job to be run and `max_concurrent` is the max number of tasks that can be run concurrently.

observations.expected: With 2 tasks and a limit of 3, once 2 tasks have started, an interrupt leaves every started task's cleanup finished before the call returns, never more than 3 run at once, and the process exits.
limits: Tasks still queued when the interrupt came aren't checked: the instruction doesn't say whether they may start.
Each task runs 1.5 s unless cancelled, so a runner that lets started tasks finish instead of cancelling them also passes.
One interrupt; a second one during cleanup isn't sent.
